decision.analysis: Round 1 established three reference points: resnet18 (0.9826 acc) > residual_cnn (0.9756) > compact_transformer (0.9476). The compact_transformer's poor result is almost certainly due to severe under-parameterization (hidden=48, well below the 128-256 range recommended by CCT literature). The residual_cnn and resnet18 both used hidden=32, depth=3, suggesting the search space was explored at a narrow capacity point. For round 2, I will: (1) give the compact_transformer a fair shot with hidden=128 and depth=3, which should bring it into the 1.5-3M parameter range where CCT excels; (2) push the residual_cnn to hidden=64, depth=5 to test whether additional residual blocks and width close the gap to resnet18; (3) refine the resnet18 configuration with a lower LR (0.0003), larger batch (256), slightly more depth (4), and class_weighting=true to exploit the mild 1.63× imbalance. All three use standardize normalization (mandatory given channel std 0.12-0.18), AdamW, cosine scheduling, and conservative augmentations (hflip, rotate180, brightness) to preserve tissue-orientation cues. Weight decay is kept at 1e-4 to avoid excessive regularization. The three candidates span the architecture spectrum (transformer, mid-depth CNN, deep CNN) at meaningfully different capacity points, providing a clear comparative signal.

candidates.rationale: Round-1 compact_transformer used hidden=48 (far below the 128-256 CCT sweet spot) and attention pooling, yielding only 0.9476. This candidate raises hidden to 128 (divisible by num_heads=4, giving 32-dim heads), increases depth to 3 blocks, switches to cls pooling for stability, and uses mlp_ratio=4 for a 512-dim FFN. With patch_size=4 the 28x28 input yields 49 tokens, a reasonable sequence length for 3 attention layers. LR=0.001 with cosine decay and 5-epoch warmup helps the conv tokenizer learn meaningful features before attention converges. Augmentations limited to hflip and rotate180 to preserve tissue orientation. Expected parameter count ~2-3M, within the 90K-sample budget.

Round-1 residual_cnn (hidden=32, depth=3) achieved 0.9756, trailing resnet18 by ~0.7%. This candidate doubles width to 64 and increases depth to 5 residual blocks, roughly tripling capacity while staying well under 4M parameters. The deeper stack accumulates a larger receptive field (5 blocks of 3x3 stride-1 convs cover ~25x25 of the 28x28 input) without max-pooling, preserving spatial detail. Dropout raised to 0.15 to counteract the increased capacity. LR lowered to 0.0005 for the deeper network. Three conservative augmentations (hflip, rotate180, brightness) expand the effective training set without destroying orientation cues. mlp_ratio=4 gives a 256-dim FFN in the classification head. This tests whether a well-tuned mid-size CNN can match or exceed resnet18 at lower parameter cost.

Round-1 resnet18 (hidden=32, depth=3, batch=128, lr=0.0005) was the best performer at 0.9826. This refinement makes four targeted changes: (1) hidden raised to 48 for slightly wider channels; (2) depth increased to 4 for marginally more residual blocks; (3) LR lowered to 0.0003 and batch increased to 256 for more stable gradients in the larger model; (4) class_weighting enabled to address the 1.63x imbalance (classes 5 and 7 have ~7.9K samples vs ~12.9K for class 8). Three augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate180) provide geometric diversity while preserving tissue structure. Weight decay kept at 1e-4 to avoid over-regularizing the ~11M-parameter model. This candidate tests whether the round-1 resnet18 result was near-optimal or whether modest hyperparameter tuning can push past 0.985.
